title: Indian Startup Intrinsic Foundries Wins L'Oréal's 2026 Big Bang Beauty Tech Prize
excerpt: The biomanufacturing startup, which turns captured carbon into beauty ingredients, wins a funded L'Oréal pilot and a year of mentoring; fellow Indian startup Hector earns a Special Mention in Singapore.
body:
• Intrinsic Foundries, an Indian biomanufacturing startup that turns industrial carbon waste into beauty ingredients, is one of three winners of L'Oréal's 2026 Big Bang Beauty Tech Innovation Program.
  • The win brings a fully funded commercial pilot with one of L'Oréal's 40 international brands, access to 35 SAPMENA markets and a year of mentoring from L'Oréal, Accenture, Google and Meta leaders.
  • Another Indian startup, AI commerce platform Hector, earned a Special Mention at the Grand Finale in Singapore, where 10 finalists pitched.
  • Indian startups have now reached the Big Bang winners' circle three years in a row.

An Indian startup that grows beauty ingredients in algae reactors fed with captured carbon dioxide has won one of the beauty industry's biggest innovation contests. Intrinsic Foundries, a biomanufacturing company that converts industrial carbon waste into beauty actives, has been named one of three winners of L'Oréal's 2026 Big Bang Beauty Tech Innovation Program, alongside Australian startups Psyke and Uluu, according to an ANI report carried by Enterprise Digital News.

Hector, an Indian AI commerce platform, received a Special Mention at the Grand Finale in Singapore, where 10 finalists from across South Asia Pacific, the Middle East and North Africa (SAPMENA) pitched to a jury of leaders from L'Oréal, Accenture, Google and Meta. India had three of the 10 finalists, and Indian startups have now made the winners' circle three years in a row, following NeuralGarage and Live2.ai in 2024 and Sravathi AI and Without in 2025.

"Seeing Indian founders in the winners' circle for the third consecutive year proves that the next generation of beauty tech is being built right here."

— Jacques Lebel, Managing Director, L'Oréal India

Carbon in, cosmetics out

Intrinsic Foundries' Carbon to X platform cultivates microalgae in closed reactors fed with captured carbon dioxide, producing beauty actives — lipids, pigments, proteins, polysaccharides and vegan carmine — on demand and to one specification every month, the report said. The company says its reactors have run continuously for over 150 days at an industrial site, a 60 kL hub has been approved under India's BIRAC MITRA programme and it already supplies Indian cosmetic and nutraceutical brands. It has raised US$1.4 million in a round led by Transition VC.

Hector, the Special Mention winner, unifies a product's advertising into a single operating layer across marketplaces and quick commerce platforms and moves budget dynamically towards live performance. It powers 219 brands across India and the US and manages over ₹1,000 crore — more than US$100 million — in annual advertising spend, according to the report.

What the winners get

Each winner can collaborate with L'Oréal on a fully funded commercial pilot with one of the group's 40 international brands, gain access to 35 SAPMENA markets and take a year-long mentorship journey with senior leaders from L'Oréal and programme partners Accenture, Google and Meta. Successful pilots can unlock further collaboration with L'Oréal globally. The other winners work different problems: Psyke structures what AI assistants learn about brands, and Uluu makes a natural plastic alternative from farmed seaweed and saltwater for cosmetic packaging, the French Chamber of Commerce in Singapore reported.

This year's challenge, "Leading the change in Beauty Tech," covered five themes including AI-powered commerce, science for beauty and innovation for good. The programme cited NielsenIQ research that 49 per cent of consumers already receive beauty product recommendations from generative AI platforms — a shift all three winners, in different ways, are built for.
